extracted.intended_audience: newsrooms, journalists, newsroom leaders, and engagement practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: A collection of case studies, guides, and commentary about implementing audience engagement practices in newsrooms, including strategies for DEI, elections coverage, revenue, metrics, and community partnerships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience engagement is essential for newsroom DEI
rubrics_metrics.description: Most newsrooms think of diversity and inclusion work as an internal affair, but those efforts won’t succeed in a bubble.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame DEI work as outward-facing: engage communities directly rather than treating DEI as only an internal HR/process matter. Use audience engagement to inform and validate inclusion efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invest in engagement journalism to justify ROI and sponsorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Is investing time and money in engagement journalism justifiable in an age of shrinking newsroom budgets? KXLY-TV proves that the answer is an emphatic yes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track outcomes from engagement efforts (including sponsorships and revenue opportunities) and use case studies to make the business case for continued investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizens Agenda: center people, not the horse race, in elections coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: The Citizens Agenda is a model for election coverage that puts people, not the horse race, at the center of campaign coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design election reporting around voters’ information needs (school board to national) rather than focusing on polling/horse-race narratives; ask audiences what they need to know.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use machine learning to uncover hidden audience information needs
rubrics_metrics.description: A new way for newsrooms to uncover and serve their communities’ hidden information needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply data and ML approaches to surface patterns and underserved topics in audience inputs; use these insights to shape coverage and outreach strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Network mapping (stakeholder mapping) to identify served and underserved audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Network mapping, or stakeholder mapping, is a concrete first step to identify who you are serving or underserving, and how you can commit to expanding that reach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Map relationships and stakeholders to reveal gaps in reach; use the map to plan partnerships and targeted engagement to expand service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learn from community organizing to build relationships without activism
rubrics_metrics.description: Community organizing can teach journalists how to build relationships with community members to make a difference—without crossing into activism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt organizing techniques for long-term relationship building while maintaining journalistic independence; be mindful of boundaries to avoid advocacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduce engagement through a stepwise culture-change guide
rubrics_metrics.description: If you’re looking to cultivate lasting culture change in your newsroom that results in producing more relevant content and authentically serving and growing your audience... In this 10-step guide, we offer practical tips and exercises to create the optimal conditions in your newsroom for meaningful engagement efforts to take root and thrive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow a structured, practical roadmap (exercises, steps) to embed engagement practices into newsroom workflows and culture to produce more relevant reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align engagement efforts with revenue while preserving mission
rubrics_metrics.description: How to connect engagement to revenue... how do we balance the need to connect our engagement work to real dollars, but also a central mission to serve the public?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop monetization approaches (e.g., sponsorships) that are aligned with editorial mission; explicitly balance commercial goals with public-service responsibilities and be transparent about trade-offs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose journalism metrics that actually count (and are countable)
rubrics_metrics.description: Choosing journalism metrics that actually count (and are countable!)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select metrics that are meaningful indicators of public service and engagement, and ensure they are practically measurable; avoid vanity metrics that don't reflect impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt an ethical framework for engagement—'Don't be an askhole'
rubrics_metrics.description: Don’t be an askhole: Toward an ethical framework for engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice ethical engagement by avoiding extractive or repetitive asks of communities, ensuring reciprocity, respecting contributors, and setting clear expectations about how audience input will be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secure newsroom buy-in for engagement work
rubrics_metrics.description: How to get engagement buy-in from your newsroom
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use internal advocacy, evidence of impact, training, and leadership support to win buy-in across beats and roles so engagement becomes part of routine editorial practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice public-powered journalism
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design journalism processes that incorporate public input and collaboration, letting community priorities shape reporting agendas and story development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use tools and methods to pursue deeper audience engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: This report examines how newsrooms across the country are pursuing deeper audience engagement using the tools and methods provided by Hearken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage engagement platforms and structured methods (surveys, Q&As, tool-supported workflows) to systematically solicit, analyze, and act on audience input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invest in local reporting and engagement ('Local That Works')
rubrics_metrics.description: Local That Works ... focuses on a six-year project that has shed light on the extraordinary work being done in public media at the local level. It includes a profile piece on the work that Hearken has done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize local public media projects and engagement strategies that strengthen community reporting and demonstrate impact at the neighborhood/municipal level.
